goal: Give PR repair sessions the inputs they need: the failing CI log, an agent session for rebase conflicts with lease-guarded push on daemon branches, one batched session per review head, and a worktree reset to the PR head first, per D9 of docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. No user-visible change: only the repair path differs.

acceptance.assertion: Source BR-GAP-C1, BR-GAP-C4; meet D9 in docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-sched-pr-repair.test.ts and tests/loop-daemon-repair.test.ts with fake GitHub and git. Done looks like: the CI repair prompt contains the failing check's bounded log excerpt and details URL, and the PR worktree is fetched and reset to the PR head before the session. Negative: a log fetch failure escalates and starts no session. Bound: the excerpt never exceeds its byte limit.

Source BR-GAP-C2; meet D9 conflict bullet in docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-sched-pr-repair.test.ts, characterization first. Done looks like: a conflicted rebase keeps the conflicted tree and runs a repair session, then pushes with --force-with-lease to the daemon-created branch. Negative: a branch outside the daemon prefixes is never force-pushed. Bound: the two-attempt cap per (head_sha, signature) still holds.

Source BR-GAP-C3; meet D9 review bullet in docs/specs/loop-agent-scheduling.spec.md. Agreed seam: tests/loop-sched-pr-repair.test.ts. Done looks like: three review comments on one PR head produce one repair session and one push, and the prompt carries each comment's path, line and diff hunk. Negative: a comment whose path is outside the TaskIntent scope_hint escalates instead of being applied.
